subject: FastPath assurance & credit stack — proposal and counteroffer
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Bartlett <tom@acme.io>; Lena Morris <lena.morris@acme.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastPath assurance & credit stack — initial proposal

Tom / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our call, attaching a concise version of the SLA tiers and two packaging options that map to the usage profile you shared:

- Option A (Retainer): Monthly retainer for guaranteed FastPath capacity, includes 99.95% regional uptime, 24x7 escalation, and 30 incident-hours of on-call coverage. Predictable unit economics and faster mean time to resolution.
- Option B (Burst credits + Base): Lower base commit, purchase burst credits for peak periods; 99.9% uptime, business-hours escalation included, 24x7 escalation as paid add-on.

I included a redline-able SOW and a simple credits_vs_retainer_calc.xlsx so you can plug in your traffic. Key asks from our side to proceed with pricing:

1) Confirm target peak QPS window and estimated monthly token volume.
2) Whether procurement prefers commit-based billing (Option A) or a credits model with top-ups (Option B).
3) Any corporate procurement constraints (PO cadence, standard redlines).

Next steps: if you prefer Option A we can provide a three-month pilot retainer rate and a DocuSign-ready SOW; if Option B we can propose a multi-month discount on credits volume.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Tiers_v2.pdf, SOW_draft_ACME.docx, credits_vs_retainer_calc.xlsx

Best,

Rachel Kim

Rachel —

Appreciate the summary and attachments. Quick feedback from our side after an internal read:

- We like the retainer predictability, but the initial retainer commitment in Option A is higher than we expected given our conservative Q2 forecast.
- Option B looks attractive if we can get a higher discount on credits at a 6-month minimum spend.
- Critical for us: 24x7 escalation with a guaranteed 30-minute response SLA for P0s, and a named escalation contact in Redwood. Can you confirm staffing for that?

Procurement also asked for a visible crediting policy for SLA breaches (how credits are calculated and applied). Can you provide a worked example?

Thanks — want to get this to legal this week.

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Systems

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 at 10:03 AM Tom Bartlett <tom@acme.io> wrote:
> Critical for us: 24x7 escalation with a guaranteed 30-minute response SLA for P0s, and a named escalation contact in Redwood. Can you confirm staffing for that?

Tom —

Short answer: yes, we can provide 24x7 on-call coverage with a named escalation engineer for your account as part of an enhanced retainer. The tradeoffs we typically present (and I included in the calc sheet) are:

- Named-oncall + 30-min P0 response requires an elevated retainer (blended monthly uplift) or a higher per-credit price for 24x7 rapid-response.
- We can substitute a 24x5 named rotation for a lower uplift if your P0 volume is expected to be very low.

Worked example (quick):
- If you take Option A with a $40k/mo retainer, named-oncall + 30-min P0 is included; SLA credit policy: single P0 incident that breaches availability yields a prorated credit equal to (incident_minutes / total_region_minutes) * monthly_retainer * impact_factor. For SEV1 incidents with customer-impacting outage >5 mins, impact_factor = 1.5.

I've also sketched a hybrid: three-month pilot retainer at 25% off list + 12% credit discount on burst top-ups for the pilot — this lowers your runway risk while keeping FastPath guarantees. See credits_vs_retainer_calc.xlsx.

If procurement wants, we can draft a short clause for the credit calc so it appears in SOW.

—Karthik
Head of Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00

Tom / Rachel —

Adding a couple implementation and escalation details from an ops perspective:

- Named escalation contact: we will provide a primary named engineer + one backup. Contacts are on-call and reachable via a dedicated Slack channel and our incident bridge.
- Response windows: we can commit to 30-min initial response for P0s and a 2-hour response for P1s when the enhanced retainer is in place. For the credits model, P0 initial response becomes 1 hour unless you purchase the rapid-response add-on.
- Post-incident RCA and playbook updates included for any P0 that impacts availability >15 minutes.

I attached a short SLO illustration and the SOW redline suggestions in-line. If you want, we can bake the credit calc into a single table in the SOW to keep legal happy.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Tiers_v2.pdf (annotated)

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks all — helpful clarity. Procurement is okay to run Option A as a three-month pilot at the discounted retainer you suggested (25% off) provided:

- The SLA credit calculation is explicitly documented in the SOW.
- We get the named escalation contact and 30-minute P0 initial response.
- DocuSign-ready SOW & an invoice schedule that aligns with our PO process.

Rachel — please route the DocuSign link and I'll get procurement to sign once legal signs off on the credit table. Appreciate the flexibility on pilot pricing — this should get us to a 6–12 month decision point.

Tom
